paper.title: Provably and Practically Efficient Neural Contextual Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Neural contextual bandit (reward in NTK RKHS, smooth activations sigma_s)
unmapped: Kernel is the neural tangent kernel of an L-layer fully connected net with activation sigma_s(u)=max(0,u)^s
Contexts x_{t,a} lie on the hypersphere S^{d-1}; K context-action vectors revealed each round, chosen arbitrarily
Learner uses an overparameterized neural net trained by gradient descent
settings.definition_quote: at each discrete sequential step $t=1,2,\dots, T$, for each action $a\in[K]$, a context vector $\bfx_{t}\in \cX$ is revealed ... receives the corresponding reward $r_{t} = h(\bfx_{t, a_t})+\xi_t$ ... (i) The input space is the $d$ dimensional hypersphere ... (ii) The reward function $h$ belongs to the RKHS induced by the NT kernel, and $h(\bfx)\in [0, 1]$ ... (iii) $\xi_t$ are assumed to be conditionally $\nu$-sub-Gaussian

symbols.q_max: max_r q_r, largest fixed retraining batch size across the R levels

conditions: NTK Gram matrix H on all context-action pairs satisfies H >= lambda_0 I (Assumption 2(i))
reward function h has RKHS (NTK) norm S and h(x) in [0,1]
contexts on the unit hypersphere S^{d-1}
tuning: width m >= poly(T, L, K, 1/lambda, 1/lambda_0, 1/S, log(1/delta))
training epochs J = Omega_tilde(T), learning rate eta = O(1/T)
fixed batch size q_r per group

source.label: theorem:regret_guarantees
source.quote: Suppose Assumptions~\ref{ass1} and \ref{ass2} hold. Consider NeuralGCB given in Algorithm~\ref{alg:NeuralGCB}, with $R$ neural nets, as defined in~\eqref{eq:nn} with $L$ hidden layers each of width $m \geq \text{poly}(T, L, K, \lambda^{-1}, \lambda_0^{-1}, S^{-1}, \log(1/\delta))$. Suppose NeuralGCB is run with a fixed batch size for each group, then the regret~defined in~\eqref{eq:regret_def} satisfies $R(T) =\Oct( \sqrt{T \Gamma_k(T)} +  \sqrt{T \Gamma_k(T) \log(1/\delta)} +\max_rq_r\Gamma_k(T))$

results.notes: Theorem does not explicitly state 'with probability 1-delta' but the bound depends on delta and the proof uses high-probability confidence intervals; recorded as high-probability. gamma_T is the maximal information gain Gamma_k(T) of the NTK. Intro claims this yields O_tilde(T^{(2d+2s-3)/(2d+4s-4)}) when combined with info-gain bounds from Vakili et al. (2021); not recorded separately since not stated formally. Appendix also sketches an adaptive-batch bound O(sqrt(T Gamma log(1/delta)) max_r sqrt(q_r)) (not a formal statement).
